This game's been included in a bundle now. And I feel like people may overlook this gem as "bundle filler", I almost did. But when I played it I was intrigued immediately. The story was well told. And the gameplay seems tailored to making the player actually feel like they were given this powerful, experimental hacking tool. The game is mostly controlled through issuing commands to a terminal. There are visuals though, which help orient you as you ease in.

The game has a few standout moments in my mind;
- Early on, being hacked and having your GUI deleted is a really immersive and smart way to demonstrate that a lot of the game can be played purely with the terminal.
- The entirety of the Labyrinths DLC was a standout, but particularly the ending and music.
- Getting traced in this game isn't game over, you have a very cool section where you race against the clock to hack your own ISP and change your IP. 
- The ending of the story felt rewarding, it was a nice payoff.
- Extra hidden secrets you might discover throughout the game or get a few hints towards after beating it.

Really enjoyed my time with this game. The main thing I have to say is that this game truly immersed me into believing it's universe and my role in it. A big part of that was the visuals. The GUI is almost barren, but that's very intentional. Typing commands into the terminal became more natural and I became fluent in queuing the various port crackers and other commands I'd need to break into these networks. 

TL;DR: Very fun, very cool, very well-made game.
It's secretly teaching you how to use a UNIX based operating system, and being damn entertaining while doing it.

Hacknet is the most brilliant and engaging loading screen simulator i‘ve ever played !

The core gameplay is simple and yet particularly well seasoned with just enough salt and peppers to make you feel like a hooded lonely hacker in a basement frantically typing commands.

So basically, you type commands and you wait for a fancy loading animation to finish the hacking.
You have multiple tools adapted to various situations, but you will quickly find that many computer require the same approach.

But wait... here is the trick, those little programs you execute all have a different memory usage and different completion time. On the top of that, you have limited time to hack a computer before being kicked in the dos by the tracking system.
So you must find and execute the list of commands in the proper order, and sometimes, find some tricks to overcome some devices.

What‘s brilliant about Hacknet, is it‘s organic teaching. You will learn some tricks, gain a new supercool malware and the game will never explicitly tell you what to do and when you have to use them. Well of course there are some notes and tutorials but you often find yourself in situations where you snap your fingers in excitation because you just «discovered» that you can hack a remote cellphone.

The story is more appealing than it may seems at first. There are a few secrets (some of them are notoriously hard to obtain), and tons of IRC logs to remind you of those times in your teenager bedroom, when you secretly stay awake the whole night to discuss with strangers. And the music... well while it is far from my taste, i found it surprisingly adapted and sometimes quite dramatic.

Hacknet have some suprises stored and does not try to outlive it‘s gamplay. Just long enough to give you the full experience. Just enough for you to want to get seconds.
